questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose JCU based on the many marine subjects available and the unique opportunity to do fieldwork in northern Australia (e.g. a field trip collecting data on corals).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. It is easy to find JCU staff in the education central who will help in the beginning and the university has many student help services.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I think the staff in the education central helped me make sure all my details and subjects were correct in the JCU system after I arrived.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: A couple of different residential colleges. Some have individual applications but a couple of them are organized together through Unilodge. I lived at Rotary International House through Unilodge.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Shared kitchen with 6 other people (at Rotary). I cooked all my own meals. Other accommodation options had a dining hall and no option to cook your own meals (e.g. George Roberts Hall).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is an easy way to meet people in the beginning and you will be close to classes and social events. Public transport is not the easiest in Townsville so if you live off campus it might take a bit more effort to get to and from classes and social events.

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register for classes through eStudent. JCU sent emails describing the process beforehand. I registered in Denmark beforehand but it is possible to register and change classes after arriving. Some classes does, however, fill up early (e.g. Coral Reef Ecology).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is an email to get help. When in Australia, go to education central to get help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the subjects I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Register from home and early if you want a popular subject. You can change your mind and registration until the end of the first week of the semester.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took only level 3 BA courses. At JCU they are taught together with master students so the lectures and workshops are at MA level. The difference between the BA and MA students is in assignments and exams. MA students had more assignments and typically more difficult or higher expectations from professors.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More assignments and tests, and they count towards the final grade. The final exam only counted for 30-40% of my grade. The style of teaching was a mix of lectures and tutorials/workshops (similar to many courses at JCU). The reading material in all my classes was research papers (no books).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BC3203 Bioinformatics
MB3190 Coral Reef Ecology
MB3200 Marine Conservation Biology
MB3270 Coastal, Estuarine and Mangrove Ecosystems

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Marine Conservation Biology was great and had some interesting assignments. It was my favorite course. 

Coral Reef Ecology was really interesting and has a field trip to Orpheus Island to collect data for an assignment about coral reef population structure. Really fun field trip and amazing to learn about corals while living so close to GBR.

The bioinformatics class was great and the professor is really good at explaining everything (I had very little prior knowledge).

Coastal, Estuarine and Mangrove Ecosystems had a high workload of assignments and they could be a bit confusing. There was a one day field trip connected to an assignment but it was not very well organized and we didn’t really know what data we were supposed to collect for the assignment. I would have picked another class instead. For an exchange semester it was not worth the time and effort.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: No big costs that I remember

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food. I am vegetarian and it was cheaper to buy groceries than I expected. Tofu is cheaper in Australia than in Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Many student societies. Examples are Zoology Society, Marine Society, Finstitute and the dive club. I highly recommend to take part in societies. They host social events as well as workshops and talks. It is also possible to play sports through JCU student association. I took part in social sports where we played a new sport every week (very fun!!).

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Societies and social sports

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Trips to see the beautiful nature in Northern Queensland. Some nice spots: Magnetic Island, Crystal Creek, Daintree and Great Barrier Reef!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Student societies or sports would be good places to meet local students. Take part in the social events that are not just for international students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I don’t remember anything very challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People were incredibly open and very polite. You thank the bus driver before getting off a bus and small talk is way more common than in Denmark.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Take part in the events and find a student society that fits your interests. People are friendly and everyone wants to make friends. 

Explore the area during the weekends! There are so many beautiful places in North Queensland. 

Expect many assignments but don’t spend all your time working on them. Enjoy living in Australia, seeing things and making friends.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I studied there for one semester but JCU is changing to trimesters. I don’t know what will be different with classes and opportunities for field work compared to my experience.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being part of the student community at JCU and exploring nature and seeing cool wildlife with friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being so far away from family and friends. Time difference.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
